title: Expert-guided Clinical Text Augmentation via Query-Based Model Collaboration
claim: Naive and prior rewriting methods drop critical facts and hallucinate content; ours preserves critical information and rephrases only non-critical elements.
layout: 4 note panels left-to-right: original, two baselines, ours; color-coded highlights
description: Four paper-note icons sit side by side, each with a bold title above: Original note, Naive LLM-based augmentation, CATO, and Ours. The original note is a white page of clinical text. Critical medical phrases in it, such as the admission for community-acquired pneumonia and the medication instructions, are in bold blue. The Naive and CATO notes are gray. Their hallucinated or irrelevant additions are in bold red, for example 'His symptoms worsened over the past 2 days' and 'oral feedings'. Several critical details are missing from them. The Ours note is on a pink background. It keeps every critical item and changes only non-critical wording, shown in bold green: the name Mr. Smith, 'Radiographic findings', 'CAP', 'underwent mobilization', 'pyrexia' and 'dyspnea'. The eye goes first to the red and green highlights.
caption: Synthetic clinical notes generated by different LLM-based augmentation methods are shown: a simple rephrasing prompt (Naive LLM-based augmentation), prompting to rewrite the note by only changing the physician’s writing style (CATO), and our model-to-model query method (Ours). Notes generated by the Naive and CATO methods omit critical medical information (highlighted in blue) and introduce hallucinated and irrelevant content (highlighted in red). In contrast, our method preserves all medical information while only rephrasing non-critical elements (e.g., patient names, synonyms of medical terms; green), achieving safe clinical note augmentation. Note: The original note shown here is synthetic and not a real note from our used dataset.
abstract: Data augmentation is a widely used strategy to improve model robustness and generalization by enriching training datasets with synthetic examples. While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong generative capabilities for this purpose, their applications in high-stakes domains like healthcare present unique challenges due to the risk of generating clinically incorrect or misleading information. In this work, we propose a novel query-based model collaboration framework that integrates expert-level domain knowledge to guide the augmentation process to preserve critical medical information. Compared to existing LLM-based and traditional augmentation methods, our generated data significantly improves preservation of critical medical information and reduces hallucinations at both the token and concept levels. Experiments on downstream clinical prediction tasks demonstrate consistent performance gains over existing augmentation methods. This lightweight collaborative framework addresses the gap between LLM augmentation potential and the safety requirements of specialized domains.
